// Standard compare function signature among generic objects.
typedef long (*cmpfun_ptr)(const void *a, const void *b);
objects.description: Function pointer type for comparison callbacks over generic objects. Returns a long signed comparison result; parameters are two opaque pointers.
Three-valued logical enumeration representing unknown, no, and yes states, with explicit integer values -1, 0, and 1.
Sentinel C++ type intentionally unconstructible and undeletable, used to trigger compile-time errors when selecting invalid template instantiations in size-based type utilities.

C++ template metafunction mapping a byte-size to a signed integer type. Specializations provided for 0,1,2,4,8. Size 0 maps to __bad_type to prevent misuse. Note: primary template is forward-declared only; useful specializations are defined here.
C++ template metafunction mapping a byte-size to an unsigned integer type. Specializations provided for 0,1,2,4,8, with 0 mapping to __bad_type.

C++ template metafunction mapping an integer type to its unsigned counterpart. Specializations for s8/s16/s32/s64 and u8/u16/u32/u64 are provided; on 32-bit platforms also maps long to ulong. Primary template is declared but not defined for other types.
C++ type trait indicating if a type is one of the project’s unsigned integer aliases. Primary template reports 0; specializations for u8/u16/u32/u64 (and ulong on 32-bit) report 1.

C++ constexpr numeric limits wrapper for project integer aliases, providing min() and max() for each aliased type via template specializations. Primary template is declared but undefined for other types.

functions.description: Macro returning the smaller of a and b using a single-evaluation, GCC/Clang statement-expression with typeof to avoid double evaluation. Intended for use where types of a and b are comparable.
requirements: a and b must be of types that can be compared with <=.
Both a and b are evaluated exactly once; side effects are allowed but will execute once.
Relies on GNU statement-expressions and typeof (GCC/Clang extensions).
The result type follows the usual conditional operator rules applied to the saved typeof(a) and typeof(b).

functions.description: Macro returning the larger of a and b using single evaluation and typeof. Intended for comparable types.
requirements: a and b must be of types that can be compared with >.
Both a and b are evaluated exactly once.
GNU statement-expressions and typeof required.
Result type follows conditional operator rules on the saved operands.

functions.description: Macro returning the smallest of three values with single evaluation for each argument, built atop MIN-like logic.
requirements: a, b, c must be mutually comparable with <=.
Each of a, b, c is evaluated exactly once.
GNU statement-expressions and typeof required.

requirements: a, b, c must be mutually comparable with >.
Each of a, b, c is evaluated exactly once.
GNU statement-expressions and typeof required.

functions.description: Macro constraining val to the inclusive range [minval, maxval], using single evaluation of each argument.
requirements: val, minval, maxval must be types that are mutually comparable with <= and >.
minval should be less than or equal to maxval; behavior if not is still defined by comparisons but likely unintended.
Each argument is evaluated exactly once.
GNU statement-expressions and typeof required.

functions.name: ABS
functions.description: Macro returning the absolute value of x with single evaluation using typeof.
requirements: x must be of an arithmetic type supporting comparison with 0 and unary minus.
For unsigned types, result equals x.
Each argument is evaluated exactly once.
GNU statement-expressions and typeof required.

functions.name: LIKELY
functions.description: Branch prediction hint macro marking condition x as likely true. Wraps compiler builtin.
requirements: x should be a boolean or boolean-convertible expression.
Requires compiler support for __builtin_expect (GCC/Clang).

functions.name: UNLIKELY
functions.description: Branch prediction hint macro marking condition x as likely false. Wraps compiler builtin.
requirements: x should be a boolean or boolean-convertible expression.
Requires compiler support for __builtin_expect (GCC/Clang).

functions.name: ARRAY_SIZE
functions.description: Macro computing the number of elements in a at compile time when a is a true array.
requirements: a must be an actual array, not a pointer or decayed array.
Result is cast to int; very large arrays may overflow int.

functions.name: CONTAINER_OF
functions.description: Macro returning a pointer to the containing struct given a pointer to one of its members. Equivalent to Linux’s container_of.
requirements: elem_ptr must point to the member mem_name within an instance of struct_type.
mem_name must be a valid member of struct_type.
Resulting pointer is valid only if elem_ptr was obtained from a real struct_type object.
Pointer arithmetic assumes a standard-layout struct.

functions.name: TO_PTR
functions.description: Macro converting an integer-like value n to a void* via a cast to ulong then to void*. Intended for working with integer physical/virtual addresses in low-level code.
requirements: n should represent an address-sized integer value; truncation or sign issues may occur if n does not fit in ulong.
This is unsafe; only use when such brutal cast is acceptable.

functions.name: DO_NOT_OPTIMIZE_AWAY
functions.description: Macro to inhibit the compiler from optimizing away x. On GCC it uses an empty volatile asm with a read/write register constraint; on Clang it calls a helper that emits a memory clobber.
requirements: Usable with any expression convertible to void* for the GCC path via TO_PTR; on Clang, any pointer-convertible expression.
Behavior depends on compiler support for inline assembly or the provided helper.

functions.name: U32_BITMASK
functions.description: Macro producing a u32 mask with the lowest n bits set.
requirements: n must satisfy 0 <= n < 32 to avoid undefined behavior from shifting by >= 32.
If n == 0 the result is 0.

functions.name: U64_BITMASK
functions.description: Macro producing a u64 mask with the lowest n bits set.
requirements: n must satisfy 0 <= n < 64 to avoid undefined behavior from shifting by >= 64.
If n == 0 the result is 0.

functions.name: LO_BITS
functions.signature:
#if defined(BITS64)
#define LO_BITS(val, n, t) ((t)((val) & U64_BITMASK(n)))
#elif defined(BITS32)
#define LO_BITS(val, n, t) ((t)((val) & U32_BITMASK(n)))
#endif
functions.description: Macro extracting the lowest n bits of val and casting to type t. Uses U64_BITMASK or U32_BITMASK depending on target word size.
requirements: n must satisfy 0 <= n < NBITS (32 or 64 depending on build) to avoid undefined shift in the underlying bitmask.
t must be a valid target type for the cast.
val should be an integer type; non-integer types must be implicitly convertible to an integer.

functions.name: SHR_BITS
functions.signature: #define SHR_BITS(val, rs, t) LO_BITS( ((val) >> (rs)), NBITS-(rs), t )
functions.description: Macro right-shifts val by rs bits, then returns the lowest NBITS - rs bits cast to type t, in a -Wconversion-safe pattern.
requirements: rs must satisfy 0 <= rs < NBITS to avoid undefined behavior from overshifting.
t must be a valid target type for the cast.
val should be an integer type; shifting follows C rules for signedness.

functions.name: IN_RANGE
functions.description: Macro checking whether addr is within the half-open interval [begin, end).
requirements: addr, begin, end must be types supporting <= and < comparisons with each other.
Assumes a strict weak ordering consistent across the three values.

functions.name: IN_RANGE_INC
functions.description: Macro checking whether addr is within the closed interval [begin, end].
requirements: addr, begin, end must be types supporting <= comparisons with each other.
Assumes a strict weak ordering consistent across the three values.

unharnessable_functions.name: LO_BITS
unharnessable_functions.reason: Macro is only defined when specific compile-time flags (BITS32 or BITS64) are set; the harness cannot assume those configuration macros.

unharnessable_functions.name: SHR_BITS
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on LO_BITS and NBITS; without guaranteed build-time configuration macros the definition may be unavailable or semantically incorrect.
